findings.issue_text: `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` is not assignable to the stored `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` union because `scope: "team"` can omit required `teamId`, causing `this.options = options` to fail type-checking

goldens.comment: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` is not assignable to the stored `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` union because `scope: "team"` can omit required `teamId`, causing `this.options = options` to fail type-checking

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the constructor parameter type changed from `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` to `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` (line 58). Looking at the type definitions, `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` has `teamId?: number` (optional), while `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` is a discriminated union where `scope: 'team'` requires `teamId: number`. The assignment `this.options = options` (line 63) assigns a `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` to `this.options` which is typed as `InsightsBookingServiceOptions | null`. When `scope: 'team'` but `teamId` is undefined, this creates a type mismatch since the union requires `teamId` to be present for team scope. This is a real type safety issue.
